intent: Move all five sensors forward from y = 0.06 m to y = 0.07 m, as the Integrator's trigger rule specifies, and keep the x spread (+/-0.024 m), 12 mm footprint, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.14 by 0.16 m body and 0.6 kg mass unchanged. I changed the forward offset alone so the result isolates look-ahead. I expect slalom max_error at or below 0.06 m, slalom progress above 0.28, and s-bend completion at or above 0.85 of runs. I am considering, but not committing to, a wider spread (+/-0.032 m) only if slalom line losses rise above 2 per run with progress below 0.2. I would also hold mass at 0.6 kg, since s-bend completion has held up well.
learning: Iteration 4 showed that the 0.6 kg mass change plus the Integrator's controller changes lifted the s-bend to 18 of 20 and slalom progress to 0.28, without line-loss growth. The remaining slalom failure is a small max_error excess (0.0638 m) with few line losses, which points to late reaction rather than sensing. Hypotheses for this race: (1) y = 0.07 m brings slalom max_error to 0.06 m or below; (2) oval steering oscillation rises only modestly (stays below about 0.3); (3) line_loss_events stay at or below 2 per run on all tracks. If (1) holds and the slalom completes, the next lever is controller tuning, not geometry. If oval or s-bend completion drops, I will revert to y = 0.06 m.
rationale:
Iteration 4 (0.6 kg, otherwise unchanged) is the best race so far at 649.6, up from 575.8. The oval completes 20 of 20 with max_error 0.0139 m. The s-bend completes 18 of 20 (up from 12), so the 0.6 kg mass is clearly not hurting it, and the revert-to-0.8 kg trigger (s-bend completion below 0.3) does not fire. The slalom still fails 0 of 20, but progress rose to 0.278 (from 0.198) and its max_error is 0.0638 m, still just above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Line losses on the slalom are 1.05 per run, well under the 2-per-run threshold, so the sensor spread is not the limit.

The Integrator's rule is explicit: if slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with line losses at or below 2 per run, the next lever is the forward offset y = 0.07 m with the spread unchanged. Both conditions hold (0.0638 m and 1.05), so I am taking that step. The widen-spread trigger (line losses above 2 with progress below 0.2) does not fire, so x stays at +/-0.024 m. Body, wheels, track, sensor size and mass stay as they are, so the offset is the only geometry change.

Expected result: slalom max_error falls toward or below 0.06 m as look-ahead grows from 60 mm to 70 mm, slalom progress rises further, and line losses stay near 1 per run. The main risk is overshoot on the oval and s-bend, where more look-ahead could increase steering oscillation (currently 0.21 on the oval). I accept that risk because the oval has a large margin on completion and max_error.
